title: Molecular mechanism leading to human coronary atherosclerosis assessed by proteomic analysis and RNA sequences.
authors: Parker, Sarah J; Mao, Chunhong; Caudell, David L; Seals, Austin Lyle; Wang, Yizhi; Green, Thomas D; McClung, Joseph M; Maxwell, Joshua T; Roddey, Jacolby T; Shakeriastani, Kiarash; Wu, Chiung-Ting; Lu, Yingzhou; Kim, Do-Kyun; Fert-Bober, Justyna; Du, Dongping; Bhat, Archana; Sundararaman, Niveda; Ayres, Matthew; Pandey, Rakhi; Bhardwaj, Saurabh; Karere, Genesio M; Troxclair, Dana; Jackson, Fannie; Love, Gordon L; Vander Heide, Richard; Hixson, James; Van Eyk, Jennifer E; Wang, Yue; Herrington, David
one_liner_zh: 该文通过蛋白质组学和RNA测序分析冠状动脉粥样硬化早期分子变化，虽涉及转录因子MLXIPL调控，但核心是疾病分子表型与调控网络，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atherosclerosis results from cellular and extracellular changes in the arterial wall, preceded by molecular shifts that initiate disease and drive tissue conversion, yet these changes are not yet fully described. More data are needed concerning these early changes in the coronary artery molecular landscape that signify the initiation of atherosclerosis and the subsequent tissue pheno-conversion to atherosclerotic plaque. This report summarizes results from a large biorepository of human coronary artery tissue, applying state-of-the-art omics technology, advanced data analytic methods, and an arterial organoid model system to predict molecular dynamics and identify potential regulatory mechanisms that could interrupt molecular changes that contribute to the earliest stages of disease pathogenesis. The long-term goal of this effort is to identify and develop new therapies to further mitigate the persistently high burden of clinical coronary disease. METHODS: Mass spectrometry-based proteomic analysis and RNA sequencing (RNASeq) were used to analyse proximal coronary arterial samples from young adults who died of trauma with no ante mortem suspicion of coronary disease [n = 322, mean age (range): 34.1 years (15-59); sex: M-239, F-83; race: W-218, B-88, other-16]. Despite the absence of clinical disease, 56% of samples had morphologic evidence of pre-clinical atherosclerosis. Analyses of the proteomic data (n = 1900 proteins) using state-of-the-art dimensionality reduction and deconvolution techniques generated an estimate of molecular disease progression (e.g. pseudo-time) and identified selected proteomic latent features (LFs) (i.e. large groups of co-ordinated proteins) associated with its initiation and progression. Computational genomics, machine learning models, and multi-omic network mapping of these proteomic LFs and associated mRNA gene transcripts suggested potential transcriptional regulators which were subsequently confirmed in publicly available single-cell coronary artery data. The effects of one of the leading regulatory transcription factors (TFs), MLXIPL, predicted to regulate two LFs, were further validated in a human arterial cell organoid model system. RESULTS: Four proteomic LFs, composed of n = 100 signature proteins/LF, exhibited distinct patterns with respect to disease progression [false discovery rate (FDR) P < .01]. These LFs illuminate the earliest changes in the arterial proteome during tissue pheno-conversion from normal coronary artery to atherosclerotic plaque, including dramatic declines in mitochondrial energy biosynthesis proteins, evidence of vascular unit activation (including pericytes), and neurovascular and neuroimmune modulation (all FDR P < .01). These early changes preceded the expected immune cell recruitment and innate immune response characteristic of atherosclerotic plaque formation. Analysis of transcriptional regulatory networks identified from RNASeq data highlighted both known and novel TFs and master regulators of LF proteins that may drive the initial and early stages of disease progression. Publicly available single-cell RNASeq data from normal and atherosclerotic coronary arteries validated the LFs and several of their likely master transcriptional regulators (all P < .01); and manipulation of the levels of one of top regulatory TFs, MLXIPL, in human arterial cell organoids resulted in the expected changes in expression of the proteins associated with its two targeted LFs (P = .0003 and P < .00001, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: The unique nature of this human coronary biorepository with samples ranging from entirely normal to mature pre-clinical atherosclerotic plaque facilitated prediction of molecular disease progression and identification of several potential transcriptional regulators for further evaluation as potential novel targets to interrupt early initiation and progression of atherosclerotic coronary disease.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：动脉粥样硬化源于动脉壁细胞和细胞外变化，其前驱是启动疾病并驱动组织转化的分子变化，然而这些变化尚未被完全描述。关于冠状动脉分子景观中这些早期变化的数据仍不足，这些变化标志着动脉粥样硬化的起始及随后组织表型向动脉粥样硬化斑块的转化。本报告总结了一个大型人冠状动脉组织生物样本库的结果，应用最先进的组学技术、先进的数据分析方法以及动脉类器官模型系统，以预测分子动力学并识别可能中断疾病发病机制最早阶段分子变化的潜在调控机制。这项工作的长期目标是识别和开发新疗法，以进一步减轻临床冠状动脉疾病持续高负担。方法：采用基于质谱的蛋白质组学分析和RNA测序（RNASeq）分析年轻成年创伤死亡者（生前无冠状动脉疾病怀疑）的冠状动脉近端样本 [n = 322，平均年龄（范围）：34.1岁（15-59）；性别：男-239，女-83；种族：白人-218，黑人-88，其他-16]。尽管无临床疾病，56%的样本具有临床前动脉粥样硬化的形态学证据。使用最先进的降维和解卷积技术对蛋白质组学数据（n = 1900个蛋白质）进行分析，生成了分子疾病进展的估计（如伪时间），并识别了与其起始和进展相关的选定蛋白质组学潜在特征（LFs）（即大型协调蛋白质组）。计算基因组学、机器学习模型以及这些蛋白质组学LFs和相关mRNA基因转录本的多组学网络映射提示了潜在的转录调控因子，随后在公开可用的单细胞冠状动脉数据中得以确认。预测调控两个LFs的主要调控转录因子（TFs）之一MLXIPL的效果，在人类动脉细胞类器官模型系统中得到进一步验证。结果：四个蛋白质组学LFs，每个由n = 100个特征蛋白质组成，在疾病进展方面表现出不同模式 [错误发现率（FDR）P < .01]。这些LFs揭示了正常冠状动脉向动脉粥样硬化斑块组织表型转化过程中动脉蛋白质组的最早变化，包括线粒体能量生物合成蛋白质的显著下降、血管单位激活（包括周细胞）的证据，以及神经血管和神经免疫调节（所有FDR P < .01）。这些早期变化先于预期的免疫细胞募集和动脉粥样硬化斑块形成特征性的先天免疫反应。从RNASeq数据中识别的转录调控网络分析，突出了已知和新颖的TFs及LF蛋白质的主调控因子，这些可能驱动疾病进展的初始和早期阶段。公开可用的正常和动脉粥样硬化冠状动脉单细胞RNASeq数据验证了LFs及其几个可能的主转录调控因子（所有P < .01）；在人类动脉细胞类器官中操纵顶级调控TF之一MLXIPL的水平，导致与其两个靶向LFs相关蛋白质表达出现预期变化（分别为P = .0003和P < .00001）。结论：该人冠状动脉生物样本库的独特性，样本范围从完全正常到成熟的临床前动脉粥样硬化斑块，促进了分子疾病进展的预测，并识别了几个潜在的转录调控因子，以供进一步评估作为中断动脉粥样硬化冠状动脉疾病早期起始和进展的潜在新靶点。
